name: Nation of Ulysses
label: Dischord
lede: Not a band, they insisted, but a political party: five DC kids with a manifesto, a trumpet, and a plan to secede from rock and roll.

eras.title: Ulysses, then a nation
eras.text: In a DC scene that had spent the '80s arguing about sincerity, a group of teenagers showed up talking like a revolutionary cell. They started as a quartet called Ulysses; a second guitarist turned them into a Nation.

years.p: [[Ian Svenonius|0ef9be87-0dbe-4551-a526-f3f6891a2e9d]] on vocals and trumpet, Steve Kroner on guitar, Steve Gamboa on bass, [[James Canty|ffc732f4-15a3-42e1-a498-965c1d793e35]] on drums.

years.h: [[Tim Green|19b6bda7-fbb1-4a45-a3c7-687114167e8c]] joins, and the party gets its name
years.p: A second guitarist, and a new name to match the ambition: The Nation of Ulysses.

eras.title: The sassiest boy in America
eras.text: Before they'd released a note, Nation of Ulysses had a doctrine. The zine Ulysses Speaks mixed '60s radicals, French Situationists and juvenile delinquency into what they called the Ulysses Aesthetic, handed out at shows and sent by mail over nine issues.

years.p: Svenonius writes most of it, Green helps with layout. Dischord's own bio describes the band the way the zine did: a violent separatist political party operating out of Washington.

q: To create a space of liberation where anything's possible.
years.h: Sassy crowns its first Sassiest Boy in America
years.p: The teen magazine picks Svenonius, with no official record out yet. He uses the space to call rock a corrupt medium.
years.xp: It was a perfect collision: a glossy magazine for teenage girls and a singer who talked like a pamphlet. Svenonius told Sassy the band wanted a space where anything was possible and dismissed traditional rock groups outright.

eras.title: Thirteen points
eras.text: The records finally came, fast and wiry and full of slogans, with song titles that read like party platform planks. Live, it was closer to a riot than a recital.

years.p: Three songs. They later ride along as bonus tracks on the 13 Point Program CD.

years.h: 13 Point Program to Destroy America · Dischord No. 57
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear in January with [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] of [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]] and Ian MacKaye. Sixteen tracks, among them Look Out! Soul Is Back, Hot Chocolate City and You're My Miss Washington, D.C.
play: A Kid Who Tells On Another Kid is a Dead Kid

years.p: Svenonius described the shows as masochistic, cacophonous and violent. He broke his arm, his leg and his head at various points along the way.

years.h: The Birth of the Ulysses Aesthetic 7" · Dischord No. 62
years.p: Three more songs with Janney producing, subtitled the synthesis of speed and transformation.

eras.title: Plays pretty, then the nation dissolves
eras.text: The second album was sharper and stranger, with more soul and more jazz in it. Then Nirvana happened, the ground moved, and the party voted itself out of existence.

years.p: Produced by MacKaye at Inner Ear. The Kingdom of Heaven Must Be Taken By Storm, The Sound of Jazz To Come, Presidents of Vice: the titles alone are a manifesto.

years.h: Nine hours in Memphis with Primal Scream
years.p: On tour with [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]], after a badly promoted Memphis show, the band runs into [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]]. They cut five songs together in nine hours: the Memphis Demos, including N-Sub Ulysses, Shakedown and Mockingbird, Yeah.
years.xp: The pairing was pure accident: a bad turnout, a chance meeting, and a studio. Several of the songs they cut that day are the same ones that anchor Plays Pretty for Baby.

years.p: Steve Kroner leaves during the recording of the third album. The other four keep going.
The four-piece records its last songs to four-track half-inch tape at The Embassy, with MacKaye. Nobody hears them for eight years.

q: The epoch changed with the advent of digital music and the Nirvana explosion.
years.p: Nation of Ulysses break up. Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa start the short-lived Cupid Car Club.
years.xp:
Svenonius has blamed the timing, not the members: digital music was arriving, Nirvana had cracked the underground open, and what came next was indie rock, which he called a vacuous form.

Kroner was already gone. The last songs sat on four-track tape until Dischord released them as The Embassy Tapes in 2000.

eras.title: The party in exile
eras.text: Nation of Ulysses never reformed, but its members never stopped. Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa carried on together in The Make-Up, Green became a producer, and the final tapes finally came out.

years.p: Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa's next group, running until 2001. Tim Green goes on to engineer and produce, and to play in [[The Fucking Champs|e786319e-c2df-4409-8e92-55fac38b5841]].
The September 1992 sessions, eight years late. The sound of a third album that never got finished.
One of several bands to follow, with Chain and the Gang and Escape-ism later on.
Svenonius's first book of essays. The Ulysses Speaks voice, now between hard covers.
Svenonius hosts an interview show on VBS.tv through 2010, talking to artists in places as grand as the Guggenheim.

years.h: Supernatural Strategies for Making a Rock 'n' Roll Group
years.p: A how-to guide from the man who spent 1990 trying to destroy rock and roll.
